name: KSZ8081RNACA-TR
title: 10BASE-T/100BASE-TX Ethernet PHY with RMII
summary: A one-port Fast Ethernet physical-layer transceiver for CAT-5 twisted pair, 10 and 100 Mb/s in half or full duplex, talking to a MAC over RMII and managed over MDC/MDIO. It runs from one 3.3 V supply, makes its own 1.2 V core rail, accepts 1.8, 2.5 or 3.3 V digital I/O, and carries the line terminations on chip. The RNA version starts up taking a 25 MHz crystal and sending the 50 MHz RMII clock to the MAC; the RND version starts up taking a 50 MHz clock on XI. Both come in a 24-pin 4 mm x 4 mm QFN.
key_figures: 10BASE-T and 100BASE-TX, half and full duplex, IEEE 802.3
RMII v1.2, 50 MHz reference clock out (RNA default) or in (RND default)
3.135 V to 3.465 V on VDDA_3.3; VDDIO 3.3, 2.5 or 1.8 V
47 mA typ at 100BASE-TX full traffic; 41 mA typ at 10BASE-T
24-pin QFN, 4 mm x 4 mm, exposed ground paddle

notes: Order code fields: KSZ8081, then R for RMII, N for the 24-pin QFN, A (25 MHz in, 50 MHz clocks out) or D (50 MHz clock in), then CA for commercial or IA for industrial temperature.

pins.name: VDD_1.2
pins.function: Core supply at 1.2 V, made by the on-chip regulator. Bypass to ground with 2.2 µF and 0.1 µF.

pins.name: VDDA_3.3

pins.name: RXM

pins.name: RXP
pins.function: Line pair, positive side; receives in MDI mode, transmits in MDI-X mode.

pins.name: TXM
pins.function: Line pair, negative side; transmits in MDI mode, receives in MDI-X mode.

pins.name: TXP
pins.function: Line pair, positive side; transmits in MDI mode, receives in MDI-X mode.

pins.name: XO
pins.function: Crystal drive output for a 25 MHz crystal. Left open when XI is fed by an oscillator or other clock.

pins.name: XI
pins.function: Reference clock input: a 25 MHz ±50 ppm crystal, oscillator or clock in 25 MHz mode, a 50 MHz ±50 ppm oscillator or clock in 50 MHz mode. At power-up the RNA expects 25 MHz on XI and the RND 50 MHz; either can be switched afterwards with register 1Fh bit 7.

pins.name: REXT
pins.function: Transmit current set: 6.49 kΩ to ground.

pins.name: MDIO
pins.function: Management data in and out. Open-drain with a weak internal pull-up; needs an external 1.0 kΩ pull-up.

pins.name: MDC
pins.function: Management clock input; MDIO is timed to it.

pins.name: RXD1
pins.function: RMII receive data bit 1, timed to the 50 MHz reference clock.

pins.name: RXD0
pins.function: RMII receive data bit 0, timed to the 50 MHz reference clock.

pins.name: VDDIO
pins.function: Digital I/O supply, 3.3 V, 2.5 V or 1.8 V.

pins.name: CRS_DV/PHYAD[1:0]
pins.function: RMII carrier sense and receive data valid output. During reset it is the PHY address strap, latched as reset is released.

pins.name: REF_CLK
pins.function: In 25 MHz mode, the MAC's 50 MHz RMII clock, sent out. In 50 MHz mode it is unused and left open. The RNA powers up in 25 MHz mode, the RND in 50 MHz mode; register 1Fh bit 7 changes either.

pins.name: RXER
pins.function: RMII receive error output. It must read low as reset is released for normal operation; an external pull-down keeps a MAC input from pulling it high. If it latches high, register 16h bit 15 clears the resulting factory test mode.

pins.name: INTRP
pins.function: Programmable interrupt output. Open-drain with a weak internal pull-up; needs an external 1.0 kΩ pull-up.

pins.name: TXEN
pins.function: RMII transmit enable input.

pins.name: TXD0
pins.function: RMII transmit data bit 0, timed to the 50 MHz reference clock.

pins.name: TXD1
pins.function: RMII transmit data bit 1, timed to the 50 MHz reference clock. In NAND tree mode it is the tree's output.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground.

pins.name: LED0/ANEN_SPEED
pins.function: LED output, programmed by register 1Fh bits 5:4; low turns the LED on. During reset it is the strap for auto-negotiation enable and speed, latched into register 0h bits 12 and 13 as reset is released.

pins.name: RST#
pins.function: Chip reset input, active low.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Exposed paddle on the underside: ground.

circuits.title: Power and ground connections
circuits.description: One 3.3 V rail feeds the chip. VDDIO takes it directly, VDDA_3.3 takes it through a ferrite bead, and each of the two has 22 µF and 0.1 µF to ground at the pin. VDD_1.2 is the chip's own regulated core rail and takes 2.2 µF and 0.1 µF. Pin 22 and the paddle both go to ground. This is the connection for 3.3 V I/O.

circuits.title: Power-on reset circuit
circuits.description: For a reset that follows the supply: 10 kΩ from VDDIO charges 10 µF on RST#, holding the chip in reset while the rail comes up. A 1N4148 sits across the resistor, anode at RST# and cathode at VDDIO.

circuits.title: Reset circuit driven by a CPU or FPGA
circuits.description: The power-on RC network of 10 kΩ, 10 µF and a discharge diode stays on RST#, and a CPU or FPGA reset output pulls the node low through D2 for a warm reset after power-up. D2 is there when the two chips run different VDDIO; then it is to be a low-drop part (VF under 0.3 V, a BAT54 or MSS1P2L for instance), or a level shifter takes its place. With equal VDDIO on both chips, the usual case, D2 is left out and the output wired straight to RST#.

circuits.title: LED0 with a pull-up strap
circuits.description: LED0/ANEN_SPEED wired to strap a 1 (auto-negotiation on, 100 Mb/s) for VDDIO of 3.3 V or 2.5 V. The LED and its 220 Ω resistor run from VDDIO into LED0, which sinks current to light it; a 4.7 kΩ resistor from VDDIO to the pin sets the strap.

circuits.title: LED0 with the strap left floating
circuits.description: LED0/ANEN_SPEED with only the LED on it for VDDIO of 3.3 V or 2.5 V. The LED and its 220 Ω resistor run from VDDIO into LED0, which sinks current to light it; with no strap resistor the internal pull-up gives a 1.

circuits.title: LED0 with a pull-down strap
circuits.description: LED0/ANEN_SPEED wired to strap a 0 (auto-negotiation off, 10 Mb/s) for VDDIO of 3.3 V or 2.5 V. The LED and its 220 Ω resistor run from VDDIO into LED0, which sinks current to light it; a 1 kΩ resistor from the pin to ground sets the strap.

circuits.title: 25 MHz crystal on XI and XO
circuits.description: A 25 MHz ±50 ppm crystal between XI and XO with 22 pF from each pin to ground, the reference for RMII 25 MHz clock mode.

circuits.title: 25 MHz oscillator on XI
circuits.description: A 25 MHz ±50 ppm oscillator drives XI for RMII 25 MHz clock mode; XO is left open.

circuits.title: 50 MHz oscillator on XI
circuits.description: A 50 MHz ±50 ppm oscillator drives XI for RMII 50 MHz clock mode; XO is left open.

circuits.title: Line interface through magnetics to an RJ-45
circuits.description: TXP/TXM and RXP/RXM each drive one winding of a 1:1 centre-tapped transformer with a common-mode choke on the line side. Because the drivers are voltage-mode and set the pairs' common-mode voltage themselves, the two PHY-side centre taps go to no supply: each has its own 0.1 µF to signal ground, kept apart since the transmit and receive pairs sit at different common-mode voltages. On the cable side, the two line centre taps and the unused pairs 4-5 and 7-8 each go through 75 Ω to one node, returned to chassis ground by 1000 pF rated 2 kV. Terminations for the pairs are inside the chip.

parts.value: 1:1 CT transformer pair with common-mode chokes

notes: T1 pins: TD+, TCT, TD- are the PHY-side winding of the transmit channel and TX+, TXCT, TX- its line side after the choke; RD+, RCT, RD- and RX+, RXCT, RX- likewise for the receive channel. TD+ and TX+ are the dotted ends.

circuits.title: RMII to a MAC in 25 MHz clock mode
circuits.description: The PHY runs from a 25 MHz crystal on XI/XO with 22 pF load capacitors and sends the 50 MHz reference clock from REF_CLK to the MAC. Receive (CRS_DV, RXD1:0, RXER) goes to the MAC and transmit (TXEN, TXD1:0) comes from it. The RNA starts in this mode; the RND needs register 1Fh bit 7 set to 1.

circuits.title: RMII to a MAC in 50 MHz clock mode
circuits.description: One 50 MHz oscillator clocks both the PHY at XI and the MAC at its REF_CLK input; the PHY's own REF_CLK pin is unused. The data lines run as in 25 MHz mode. The RND starts in this mode; the RNA needs register 1Fh bit 7 set to 1.

circuits.title: Two PHYs back to back as a 100BASE-TX copper repeater
circuits.description: Two KSZ8081RNA/RND share one 50 MHz oscillator on XI, and each one's receive outputs drive the other's transmit inputs: CRS_DV to TXEN, RXD1 to TXD1, RXD0 to TXD0. Both are set to the 50 MHz clock mode (the RNA by setting register 1Fh bit 7) and register 16h bits 6 and 1 are both set to 1 for back-to-back mode. Each line side goes to its own magnetics and cable.

operation.text: The RNA and RND differ only in their power-up clock mode. The RNA comes up in RMII 25 MHz mode: a 25 MHz crystal or clock on XI, and the 50 MHz RMII clock sent out of REF_CLK to the MAC. The RND comes up in RMII 50 MHz mode, taking a 50 MHz clock on XI and leaving REF_CLK unused. Register 1Fh bit 7 switches either one to the other mode after power-up.

The transmit path serialises the MAC data into a 125 MHz stream, applies 4B/5B coding and scrambling, converts NRZ to NRZI and drives MLT-3 as a current. A 6.49 kΩ 1 % resistor on REXT sets that current for a 1:1 transformer. Rise and fall are about 4 ns. The 10BASE-T waveshaping lives in the same driver.

An adaptive equaliser undoes the cable's length-dependent loss and phase distortion and keeps retuning, for instance with temperature. DC restoration then corrects baseline wander, an adaptive slicer converts MLT-3 to NRZI, a 125 MHz clock is recovered from the edges, and the data is descrambled, 4B/5B decoded and handed to the MAC in parallel.
In 100BASE-TX the data is scrambled to spread its spectrum, cutting EMI and baseline wander; the receiver undoes it. Register 1Fh bit 0 turns scrambling off.

The 10BASE-T driver shares the 100BASE-TX output and magnetics, applies waveshaping and pre-emphasis internally and reaches about 2.5 V peak, with harmonics 27 dB or more under the fundamental for an all-ones Manchester stream. On receive, a squelch rejects signals under 400 mV or with narrow pulses; above it a PLL locks and the Manchester stream is split into clock and NRZ data. The receive clock keeps running between frames.
In 25 MHz mode every internal and external clock comes from the 25 MHz crystal, oscillator or reference on XI. In 50 MHz mode they come from a 50 MHz oscillator or system clock on XI.

Auto-negotiation follows IEEE 802.3 clause 28 and picks the best mode both ends share, in the order 100BASE-TX full, 100BASE-TX half, 10BASE-T full, 10BASE-T half. If the partner does not negotiate, the PHY parallel-detects by listening for 100BASE-TX idles or 10BASE-T link pulses. It is on after power-up or reset unless the ANEN_SPEED strap is pulled down, and register 0h bit 12 turns it on or off later; when off, register 0h bit 13 sets speed and bit 8 sets duplex.

RMII v1.2 uses eight lines: TXEN and TXD1:0 for transmit, CRS_DV, RXD1:0 and RXER for receive, and the 50 MHz REF_CLK, at 10 or 100 Mb/s in half or full duplex. Data moves two bits per clock. TXEN goes high with the first preamble dibit and drops before the clock after the last; with TXEN low the PHY ignores TXD unless it is 00. CRS_DV goes high asynchronously when carrier appears (squelch passed at 10 Mb/s; two non-adjacent zeros in ten bits at 100 Mb/s), so RXD reads 00 until decoding is valid, and it falls before the clock after the frame's last dibit. RXER flags a symbol error for one or more clocks. The MAC derives COL from TXEN and CRS_DV.

Two PHYs can be joined RMII to RMII as a managed 100BASE-TX copper repeater. Both run from one 50 MHz reference on XI in 50 MHz mode, register 16h bits 6 and 1 are set to 1, and the receive lines of each go to the transmit lines of the other.

MDC and MDIO give IEEE 802.3 clause 22 access to the 16-bit registers; 0h to 8h are the standard set and the rest are vendor registers. Only PHY addresses 0h and 3h are available, chosen by the PHYAD strap on pin 15. Address 0h starts out as a broadcast address that every PHY answers, so writes to it reach all of them. Where two of these PHYs share MDIO at 0h and 3h, a broadcast write setting register 16h bit 9 in both makes 0h an ordinary address.

INTRP signals a change of PHY status so the host need not poll. Register 1Bh bits 15:8 choose which events assert it and bits 7:0 report which happened; reading the register clears them. Register 1Fh bit 9 sets its polarity, active low by default.

HP Auto MDI/MDI-X detects which pair the partner transmits on and assigns the PHY's pairs to match, so straight and crossover cables both work. It is on by default; register 1Fh bit 13 turns it off, and then bit 14 picks MDI or MDI-X. A transformer with matching transmit and receive paths is recommended for it.

Local (digital) loopback returns the MAC's transmitted frames back over RMII inside the chip, at 10 or 100 Mb/s full duplex: set register 0h bit 14 = 1, bit 12 = 0, bit 8 = 1 and bit 13 for the speed. The frames also leave on the copper port unless the transmitter is turned off with register 1Fh bit 3 for the test. Remote (analog) loopback returns a link partner's frames back down the cable, in 100BASE-TX full duplex only: force 100 Mb/s full duplex with auto-negotiation off (or negotiate to it), then set register 1Fh bit 2.

LinkMD sends a pulse down a pair and reads its reflection to find opens, shorts and impedance mismatches and the distance to them. Turn off Auto MDI/MDI-X (register 1Fh bit 13 = 1, bit 14 picking the pair), write 1 to register 1Dh bit 15, wait for it to read 0, then read the result in bits 14:13 (00 normal, 01 open, 10 short, 11 test failed) and the distance count in bits 8:0. A failed test means the link partner could not be silenced, so a reflection cannot be told from the partner's signal.

For board-level fault finding, the digital I/O pins form a chain of NAND gates ending at TXD1. Set register 16h bit 5, drive every input high, then pull each input low in the listed order and leave it low. TXD1 must change state at every step, alternating high-to-low and low-to-high; a step where it does not marks a faulty pin.
Register 1Fh bit 10 enables power-saving mode, active with auto-negotiation on and no cable. Only the transmitter, the PLL and the energy detector keep running. Off after power-up.

Writing 0 to register 18h bit 11 enables EDPD, active with auto-negotiation on and no cable. With register 10h bit 4 set the PLL also stops, leaving only the transmitter and energy detect running. Link pulses still go out at a longer interval, so that two sleeping partners with Auto MDI/MDI-X off still wake when cabled together. Off after power-up.

Register 0h bit 11 powers the device down, leaving only the management interface; clearing it resumes operation. Register 11h bit 5 additionally swaps the XI clock for an internal slow oscillator, the lowest-power state. To leave that state, clear register 11h bit 5, then clear register 0h bit 11, then software-reset with register 0h bit 15.
One 3.3 V supply runs the chip; the core's 1.2 V comes from the internal regulator on VDD_1.2. VDDA_3.3 is fed through a ferrite bead. VDDIO may be 3.3, 2.5 or 1.8 V.

The VDDIO and VDDA_3.3 ramp is to be monotonic with at least 300 µs from 10 % to 90 %, and RST# released no sooner than 10 ms after they are stable. A warm reset holds RST# low for 500 µs or more. Straps are read as reset is released, and MDC/MDIO access waits 100 µs after that.
RXER must latch low at reset. If the MAC pulls it high, the chip enters a factory test mode that writing 0 to register 16h bit 15 clears; an external pull-down on RXER avoids the case.

With 1.8 V VDDIO an LED on LED0 is not recommended. The ANEN_SPEED strap still works: 4.7 kΩ to VDDIO or open for 1, 1.0 kΩ to ground for 0. An RJ-45 with built-in LEDs at 1.8 V VDDIO needs a level shift from the 3.3 V LED side, for instance with a level-shifter part or a bipolar transistor.

The line needs a 1:1 isolation transformer, with integrated common-mode chokes where emissions are to beat FCC limits. The drivers are voltage-mode and the terminations are on chip, so the PHY-side centre taps are not tied to a supply; each goes to ground through its own 0.1 µF, separate from the other because the transmit and receive pairs sit at different common-mode voltages.
The exposed paddle is ground. The land pattern puts four thermal vias of 0.30 to 0.35 mm diameter in it, connected to ground, and four 1.00 mm x 1.00 mm stencil openings at 1.20 mm pitch.
